text:
You are on the support-desk Genkit app in this directory. Bug report: The replies that draftReply writes for customer tickets stop after the first line, usually just "Dear customer," or "Hi there,". There is no error, and the reason it reports for stopping looks normal. I expected a complete reply that explains the next steps and signs off from the support team.
Find the root cause and fix it in the app's source. Then write `answer.json` in the project root: { "file": "<path of the file that had the bug>", "snippet": "<the exact broken text you replaced, copied verbatim, one line is enough>", "cause": "<one sentence>", "evidence": "<what shows this is the cause>" }. Don't change `package.json` or add dependencies.
I should explore the workspace first to locate the draftReply code.
I'll start by locating `draftReply` and the code around it.

text: Found it — draftReply has a stop sequence set to a newline character, which cuts off generation at the first line break. I want to check if other flows share this issue, or if it's coming from the dotprompt files, so I'll grep for stopSequences across the repo.
The likely culprit is `config: { stopSequences: ['\n'] }` in `draftReply`, which halts generation at the first newline. I'll check for other stop sequences or related config before editing.

text: I want to check ai.ts for other relevant details like the default maxOutputTokens setting on the model config.
`src/ai.ts` has a comment about token caps, so I'll read it to rule out a second cause.

The actual bug is that stopSequences config in draftReply is cutting off generation early—removing that config line should fix it, since the finishReason would show "stop" either way so that check isn't the distinguishing factor.
`src/ai.ts` only sets temperature and thinking budget, so the per-call `stopSequences: ['\n']` in `draftReply` is the cause. I'll remove that line.

Now I'm preparing answer.json with the exact broken snippet properly escaped so the backslash-n sequence decodes correctly as a literal string in JSON. I'm also considering running tsc locally to verify the fix, since it's a safe, reversible check.

I also want to confirm my evidence: grepping shows the only stopSequences definition is at line 64 of flows.ts, and ai.ts's default config doesn't set it, so this is the sole source. The stop sequence `\n` matches the newline right after the greeting line, which explains why output truncates after "Dear customer," -- and the finishReason being "stop" aligns with the "looks normal" report, confirming this is indeed the root cause.
Next I'll type-check the project and write `answer.json`.

text:
The root cause was a per-call `stopSequences: ['\n']` in `draftReply` (`src/flows.ts`), which made the model stop at the first newline. I removed that line, and the project still type-checks. I did not run the flow against the model, so the fix is confirmed by reading the code rather than by a live reply.

`answer.json` is written in the project root. `package.json` and dependencies are unchanged.
